property_summary: For any inputs, calling C.transfer(...) never forwards gas-dependent reverts to the caller and therefore always returns true (completes successfully); the mutant using call{value:0}(...) can change low-level return propagation behavior so that a callee that deliberately consumes all gas in a fallback causes transfer to return false for some inputs, breaking the rule.

For every input the reference C.transfer(...) always returns true (call completes successfully), while the mutant that uses caddress.call{value:0}(...) can cause the transfer call to return false (or revert propagation difference) when interacting with a malicious callee; the rule is that transfer never fails for any callee behavior that a low-level call with empty value would expose.

For any inputs (non-empty _tos), C.transfer always completes (does not revert) and returns true when called; the mutant using caddress.call{value:0}(...) can make the external call consume all gas and cause transfer to revert or behave differently for some adversarial callee, so the mutant can break the guarantee.

For any non-empty _tos array, C.transfer(...) always returns true (completes without reverting) regardless of callee behavior; the mutant using caddress.call{value:0}(...) can cause the transfer call to return false for some malicious callee that intentionally returns false from its fallback/receive, so the property is: transfer never returns false (i.e., call succeeds) for any callee — reference satisfies it, mutant can violate it.

For any non-empty _tos input and any callee behavior, C.transfer(...) always returns true (completes successfully) when invoked; the mutant that switches to caddress.call{value:0}(...) can cause the transfer invocation to fail/return false for some adversarial callee, breaking that universal guarantee.

For any inputs (non-empty _tos), the reference contract's transfer(...) call always completes successfully and returns true (call succeeds regardless of callee failure because low-level call on a typed address propagates success boolean differently), whereas the mutant using address(caddress).call(...) can cause transfer to return false/behave differently when the callee reverts or returns failing status — so the reference always yields a true/ok result while the mutant can fail for some adversarial callee.

For every input with non-empty _tos, the reference contract's transfer(...) always completes successfully and returns true (observed as the call not reverting and returning true), while the mutant using address(caddress).call(...) can make the transfer call report failure (revert or return false) when the callee deliberately reverts; the test fuzzes the parameters and uses an adversarial Reverter callee to expose this difference.

For any non-empty _tos array and any adversarial callee, the reference C.transfer always returns true (call completes successfully), whereas the mutant using address(caddress).call(...) can cause the transfer call to report failure (return false) when a callee's fallback reverts; the test deploys a reverter helper and fuzzes inputs to find such a case.

For any non-empty _tos array and any callee address, the reference C.transfer(...) call never reverts (the external low-level call is made on a typed address variable so the caller always returns true), whereas the mutant that does address(caddress).call(...) can cause transfer(...) to revert or return a failing call boolean when the callee's fallback reverts; we assert that calling transfer does not revert for all admissible inputs using an adversarial reverter helper which the mutant would expose.

For any non-empty _tos array and any callee address, calling C.transfer(...) always returns (completes) true/does not revert; the mutant that casts to address(caddress).call(...) can cause the overall call to report failure for some adversarial callee, so the reference's transfer always yields ok=true while the mutant yields ok=false for some inputs.

For any inputs with a non-empty _tos array, the reference contract's transfer(...) always returns true (completes and yields true) even if a callee's low-level call fails silently; the mutant returns false when any callee low-level call returns false, so there exist inputs (a failing callee address and suitable _tos/_v) that make the mutant return false while the reference still returns true.

For every non-empty _tos array, the reference C.transfer(...) always returns true (it ignores callee failures), while the mutant returns false if any low-level call to the callee returns false — so there exists a callee that causes the mutant to return false but the reference still returns true.

For any non-empty _tos array, the reference C.transfer always returns true (it ignores callee failures); the mutant returns false if any low-level call to the callee returns false — so there exist inputs (a failing callee address and matching _tos/v) that make the mutant return false while the reference still returns true.

For any inputs, calling C.transfer(...) never modifies C's own storage (i.e., leaves C's state unchanged / returns successfully without altering C), because C uses external call which executes callee code in callee context; replacing call with delegatecall can run callee code in C's context and thus can change C's state (violating the invariant).

For every input, calling transfer(...) on the correct contract never changes C's own storage (no observable write by the callee into C), whereas the mutant using delegatecall can cause the callee's code to mutate C's storage for some inputs.

For any calldata, calling transfer(...) on the reference C never causes C's balance to increase (external call executes in callee context), but the mutant using delegatecall can execute payable code in the callee in C's context causing address(c).balance to increase for some inputs.

For every input, calling transfer(...) on the correct contract never causes the callee's code to execute in C's context (so a malicious helper's delegatecall payload cannot modify C's storage), but the mutant using delegatecall can cause the helper's code to run in C's context and thus mutate C's public storage for some inputs.

For every input, calling transfer(...) on the reference contract never lets the callee's code mutate C's storage variable transferCount (a public uint) — the mutant using delegatecall can cause the callee to run in C's context and increment that storage for some inputs, breaking the property.
